answer: Sybil resistance holds when each agent identity must lock a refundable bond in a scarce asset, with superlinear cost: the Nth identity from one funder costs N^2 units. One honest agent pays 1; 1,000 sybils cost 333,833,500 units total, not 1,000. A single funding jetty feeding many addresses is visible on-ledger, so the ring looks hollow: many identities, one source. Honest agents earn nectar (fee rewards) above their bond; sybils cannot, since quadratic cost outruns rewards. To break it an attacker needs truly independent funders, which just repays the scarce cost each time.
